title: Directional Lensing Residuals at Cluster Merger Shock Fronts
description: Pre-registered observational pipeline to test for a directional asymmetry in lensing convergence residuals across galaxy cluster merger shock fronts. It defines a locally normalized estimator Asig using a rotation null to isolate shock-locked signals and fits a mass+gas-pressure model outside the shock aperture to avoid circularity. Mock Bullet Cluster analogues show correct sign separation between EFC-like and ΛCDM cases with zero false positives, and the pipeline is ready for JWST κ-maps combined with Chandra thermodynamics.

effective_speed_entropy.description: EFC-motivated coupling: effective speed of light depends on local entropy S via a monotonically decreasing function \mu(S), implying extra convergence in low-entropy regions.

kappa_model.description: Projected convergence model combining dark matter (two NFW halos) and a gas component.

kappa_gas.description: Gas contribution includes a surface-density term and a pressure-proxy term, with coefficients (\alpha, \beta) fitted outside the shock aperture.

delta_kappa.description: Convergence residual used to test for departures from symmetric mass-only models.

A_shock.description: Raw directional asymmetry across the shock; positive values indicate excess residual convergence on the low-entropy (pre-shock) side.

A_sig.description: Primary locally normalized statistic using a rotation-null distribution of A_shock to isolate shock-locked asymmetry and provide robust significance.

key_results.main_finding: Pre-registered pipeline validated on synthetic Bullet Cluster analogues shows correct sign separation between EFC-like (positive) and ΛCDM-like (negative/null) cases with zero false positives; ready for JWST+Chandra application.
datasets_used: Synthetic Bullet Cluster analogues (beta-model ICM + two NFW halos)

sealed_predictions.statement: At well-resolved merger shock fronts (e.g., Bullet Cluster, Abell 2146), the pre-shock (low-entropy) side will exhibit a positive directional convergence residual, yielding A_sig > 0 and preferably A_sig > 3 with p_rot < 0.05 when JWST κ-maps are combined with Chandra thermodynamics using the pre-registered pipeline.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Applying the pipeline to JWST κ-maps and Chandra thermodynamic maps at published shock fronts and measuring A_sig ≤ 0 or failing to reach significance (p_rot ≥ 0.05) across multiple fronts.

kill_criteria: KC1: In at least two independent, high-quality cluster shock fronts (e.g., Bullet Cluster and Abell 2146) that meet the pre-registered data and geometry cuts, the measured asymmetry is non-positive and non-significant: A_sig ≤ 0 with p_rot ≥ 0.05 for each front (95% CI), ruling out a systematic low-entropy excess.

KC2: Observation of a statistically significant reversed signal at any qualifying front: A_sig ≤ -3 with p_rot < 0.05 using the pre-registered rotation-null and anti-circularity fit, contradicting the predicted pre-shock excess.

KC3: The apparent asymmetry disappears when the shock aperture is defined purely from X-ray data (blind to κ) and persists only when geometry is tuned to κ, indicating circularity; specifically, Asig drops by ≥ 3σ when reverting to the pre-registered X-ray-defined geometry.

KC4: Robustness failure: materially different κ reconstructions (independent teams or methods) applied to the same shock yield consistent null or negative Asig (all with p_rot ≥ 0.05), indicating the effect is not reconstruction-robust.

ledger_impact.holistic_analysis: This paper delivers a pre-registered, rotation-null lensing pipeline targeted at merger shock fronts, designed to isolate any entropy-locked directional excess in κ beyond symmetric mass-only expectations. It demonstrates on synthetic Bullet Cluster analogues that the Asig estimator cleanly separates EFC-like positive signals from ΛCDM-like null/negative cases with zero false positives, and is now ready for JWST κ-maps plus Chandra thermodynamics. This creates a decisive, low-circularity cluster-scale test of EFC’s entropy-coupled photon propagation without requiring new theory advances.
graph_insights: This introduces a new bridge between gravitational lensing and intracluster thermodynamics via entropy, tightly focused on Bullet Cluster–like shocks.
It targets an environment-locked, directional signal not degenerate with symmetric mass models, complementing standard cluster and cosmic-shear tests.

page_updates.new_text: Add a sealed, pre-registered pipeline for directional κ-residual asymmetry across merger shock fronts (Bullet Cluster, Abell 2146). Pipeline includes rotation-null, outside-aperture mass+pressure fit, and robustness criteria; ready for JWST κ + Chandra thermodynamics application.
page_updates.reasoning: The paper finalizes a pre-registered, implementation-ready pipeline with explicit decision criteria and robustness checks.

page_updates.new_text: Document the shock-front Asig estimator and rotation-null methodology to isolate entropy-locked lensing signals predicted by EFC. Include kill criteria for null/reversed/robustness-failure outcomes and note mock validation showing correct sign separation and zero false positives.
page_updates.reasoning: The method operationalizes an EFC-specific prediction and defines falsifiable outcomes; it should be captured in the core methods narrative.

implicit_consequences: A positive detection would directly calibrate the μ(S) amplitude governing ceff(S) in EFC using the measured Asig, constraining cluster-scale parameter space.
Execution will necessitate independent JWST κ reconstructions to meet the pipeline’s robustness criterion, effectively creating a cross-team reproducibility requirement.
A null or reversed result at two qualifying fronts would sharply constrain or falsify the entropy-coupled photon propagation sub-hypothesis within EFC.
